content.value_statement: dbt projects can become inconsistent as models, tests, and incremental logic grow. This skill provides practical patterns for organized, documented, and efficient transformations.
actual_capabilities: Organizes dbt models into staging, intermediate, and marts layers with consistent naming.
Provides source definitions with freshness, uniqueness, null, and relationship tests.
Demonstrates dimension and fact models using dbt references and warehouse SQL.
Compares incremental strategies for merge, delete and insert, and partition overwrite workflows.
Shows reusable macros, development data limits, selectors, testing commands, and documentation commands.
Documents practical conventions for materializations, schemas, model ownership, and data quality.
limitations: Examples require adaptation for each warehouse adapter, schema, and business definition.
The skill does not inspect data, execute dbt, or verify generated transformations.
Some examples require the dbt-utils package and warehouse-specific SQL functions.
It does not configure credentials, deployment platforms, or orchestration services.

use_cases.title: Structure a New Analytics Project
use_cases.description: Create clear model layers, naming rules, source definitions, and materialization defaults for a new dbt repository.
use_cases.target_user: Analytics engineers starting a dbt project

use_cases.title: Improve Data Quality Coverage
use_cases.description: Add model documentation, source freshness checks, key constraints, relationship tests, and accepted-value tests.

use_cases.title: Scale Large Warehouse Models
use_cases.description: Select incremental strategies, define reliable keys, handle late data, and limit development scans.
use_cases.target_user: Data platform leads optimizing warehouse workloads

prompt_templates.title: Plan a dbt Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dbt project structure for [business domain] using sources, staging, intermediate, and marts layers. Explain naming and materialization choices.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tests and Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these dbt model and source definitions: [details]. Propose descriptions, freshness rules, and suitable uniqueness, null, relationship, and accepted-value tests.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Incremental Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an incremental design for [model] on [warehouse]. Consider volume, unique keys, late records, updates, partitions, schema changes, and full refreshes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production dbt Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this dbt project structure and model flow: [details]. Identify layering, duplication, testing, freshness, documentation, performance, and deployment risks. Prioritize improvements.

output_examples.input: Plan model layers for Stripe payments and Shopify orders.
output: Sources: Define Stripe customers and payments, plus Shopify orders, with freshness checks.
Staging: Standardize identifiers, amounts, statuses, and timestamps in source-specific models.
Intermediate: Aggregate successful payments and order activity by customer.
Marts: Publish a customer dimension and an order fact table with tested keys.

output_examples.input: Recommend tests for a customer dimension.
output: Test the surrogate key and natural customer identifier for uniqueness and null values.
Require email when the business process guarantees it.
Restrict customer tier to approved values.
Validate nonnegative lifetime value and relationships from dependent fact models.

output_examples.input: Select an incremental strategy for late-arriving order updates.
output_examples.output: Use a merge strategy with a stable order key and an updated timestamp watermark. Include a lookback window and schedule periodic full-refresh validation.

best_practices: Adapt every example to the warehouse adapter and validate compiled SQL before deployment.
Define model grain, ownership, keys, tests, and documentation together.
Test incremental models against full-refresh results and late-arriving records.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample schemas or business rules without checking source semantics.
Do not use incremental materialization without a stable key and recovery plan.
Do not bypass staging by embedding repeated source cleanup in marts.

faq.question: Which dbt layers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers source definitions, staging models, intermediate logic, dimensions, facts, tests, documentation, and macros.

faq.question: Can it choose a materialization strategy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare views, tables, ephemeral models, and incremental strategies using your workload details.

faq.question: Does it run dbt commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance, but you must run and validate commands in your environment.

faq.question: Does it support every data warehouse?
faq.answer: The patterns are general, but SQL functions and incremental features differ by adapter.

faq.question: Does it require dbt-utils?
faq.answer: Some examples use dbt-utils tests and surrogate keys. Replace them or install the package as appropriate.

faq.question: Can it review an existing dbt project?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide project structure, model definitions, warehouse adapter, data grain, and current problems for a focused review.
